messages:
Emma: quick question — trying to wire a k8s Secret into our web chart. I put secret name/key in values.yaml but the env var ends up empty after helm upgrade. values.yaml snippet:

```
secrets:
  name: my-app-secret
  apiKey: "{{ .Files.Get "secrets/api_key" }}"   # trying this but looks wrong
```

Is this the right approach? I'm trying to avoid putting secret value into values because CI writes values files.

Raj: Don't template secret values into values.yaml. Helm's values are not evaluated as templates by default. Instead put the secret name in values and reference it from the Deployment manifest using valueFrom.secretKeyRef. Example:

```
env:
  - name: API_KEY
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: {{ .Values.secrets.name }}
        key: api_key
```

Then create the Secret resource separately (sealed-secrets / k8s secret from Terraform) with key `api_key`.

Olivia: If you really need to render template functions from values you can use `tpl` in the chart template, e.g.

```
value: {{ tpl .Values.someRenderedValue . | quote }}
```

But avoid templating raw secrets into release manifests — prefer mounting or valueFrom. Also run `helm template` locally to verify before upgrading.

Emma: ah, I see — our CI was trying to inject the secret value into values.yaml using envsubst. We should instead have Terraform create the Secret and only pass the name via env var. I'll switch the pipeline. Thanks! :relieved:

Raj: also watch out for `--set` coercion; use `--set-string` for strings with leading zeros or special chars. And `helm upgrade --install --dry-run --debug` is your friend.

Deploy Bot: Pipeline `infra/terraform` triggered a plan for `k8s-secrets` (run id 4587).

Emma: will try and report back later :thumbsup:

Olivia: lmk if you want me to pair on the CI change.
